hook: Capstone three: PDFs in, structured fields out, low-confidence cases to humans, results into your systems — **extraction at scale with honesty built in**.

scenes.title: Extraction as a typed contract: **fields, not prose**
scenes.sub: From invoices, forms, reports — to structured records
scenes.narration: The job: invoices arrive as PDFs; the system must produce records — vendor, invoice number, dates, line items, total, tax. The agent's extraction is CONTRACT-DRIVEN: a Pydantic schema per document type defines every field — name, type, and validation rule — 'total must equal sum of line items within rounding; dates parse and fall within the last year; invoice numbers match the vendor's format.' The model extracts against the schema — GA-18's response-model discipline — receiving the parsed page text, not raw PDF: a parsing layer — pdfplumber for digital PDFs, OCR for scans, with GA-14's warnings about tables and layout — converts to clean text upstream, so extraction reasons over words, not glyph positions. Two-pass for quality: a first extraction, then a VERIFICATION pass — 'check this record against the source text; list any field whose value isn't literally supported by the text' — evaluator-optimizer in miniature, catching hallucinated fields before they propagate.

scenes.title: The extraction contract, with self-verification
scenes.body:
class InvoiceLine(BaseModel):
    description: str
    quantity: Decimal
    unit_price: Decimal
    line_total: Decimal

class Invoice(BaseModel):
    vendor: str
    invoice_number: str          # pattern: INV-\d{6}
    issue_date: date
    due_date: date | None
    lines: list[InvoiceLine]
    subtotal: Decimal
    tax: Decimal
    total: Decimal

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def totals_reconcile(self):
        if abs(sum(l.line_total for l in self.lines) - self.subtotal) > Decimal("0.01"):
            raise ValueError("lines don't sum to subtotal")
        if abs(self.subtotal + self.tax - self.total) > Decimal("0.01"):
            raise ValueError("subtotal + tax != total")
        return self

async def extract(text: str) -> tuple[Invoice, list[str]]:
    inv = await llm(EXTRACT_PROMPT, text=text, response_model=Invoice)
    # verification pass: every field must be text-supported
    issues = await llm(VERIFY_PROMPT, source=text, record=inv.model_dump(),
                       response_model=list[str])
    return inv, issues   # issues feed the confidence score
annot: Pydantic validators encode business INVARIANTS — arithmetic reconciliation runs in code, not in prompt hope
The verify pass is a different prompt with a different job: find unsupported fields — separation of extraction and audit
issues are data: they drive the confidence score and the exception-queue routing
scenes.narration: Why the contract earns so much of the design: validation that lives in the schema is testable — unit-test the reconciler with wrong totals; versioned — a new invoice format is a schema version, deployed like GA-26 artifacts; and self-documenting — the field descriptions become the model's extraction instructions. The verification pass catches the extraction's signature failure — the PLAUSIBLE field: a hallucinated tax rate that arithmetic validates because the model adjusted everything to fit. Verification asks a different question — 'is this value IN THE TEXT?' — and flags 'total: 1,240' when the document says 1,420. Confidence scoring assembles the verdict: schema validation passed, verification issues empty, parsing quality good — high confidence → auto-accept; anything short → the exception queue. Confidence is COMPUTED, never self-assessed — the same external-verification principle as GA-25's routing.

scenes.title: The exception queue: **humans see only what needs eyes**
scenes.narration: High-volume extraction succeeds quietly; the exception queue is where the system earns trust. ROUTING: by confidence — computed from validation results, verification issues, and parse quality — below threshold goes to review; by field — missing critical fields, arithmetic mismatches, unparseable documents always route; nothing is silently dropped or silently guessed. The REVIEW PACKAGE is the product: the document, side-by-side with the extracted record; every flagged field highlighted with its issue — 'total didn't reconcile: lines sum to 1,410, extracted total 1,420'; the source text location for each value — the reviewer checks in seconds, not minutes. The reviewer's corrections feed back: each corrected record becomes a golden-set case — GA-20's loop at extraction scale — and correction PATTERNS aggregate: 'invoice_number misreads on this vendor's font' — a signal to improve the parse layer or add a few-shot example. The queue's METRICS are the system's quality dashboard: exception rate, top issue classes, correction rates — reviewed weekly.

items.s: Validation + verification + parse quality → score · below threshold = review, never silent guesses
Document + record + per-field issues + source locations · seconds-to-review by design
Every correction → golden case · patterns → pipeline fixes (parse layer, few-shot, schema)

scenes.narration: The economic argument for this design: humans reviewing EVERY document is the old world — expensive, slow, the bottleneck; humans reviewing FIVE PERCENT of documents is the new world — same accuracy where it matters, a fraction of the cost. But it only works if the five percent is the RIGHT five percent — which is why confidence is computed from independent signals rather than the model's mood, and why the queue's metrics get watched: a rising exception rate means the intake distribution shifted — new vendors, new formats, degraded OCR — detected in days from the dashboard rather than in months from customer complaints. Also design the fast path honestly: auto-accepted records are SAMPLED for audit — two percent re-checked — auto-acceptance without audit drifts; the sample's findings recalibrate the threshold. The queue is not an error dump; it's the system's learning organ.

scenes.title: Writing results to your systems: **the last mile, guarded**
scenes.narration: Accepted records flow into business systems — the accounting database, the CRM, the document store — and the integration step inherits every discipline. IDEMPOTENCY: each record carries a natural key — vendor plus invoice number — upserts replace rather than duplicate; re-running the pipeline is safe, the AG-02 rule at data scale. PARTIAL FAILURE: per-record results — '47 written, 1 rejected by the ERP as duplicate, 1 queued' — the batch never all-or-nothing; failed writes go to the exception queue with the target system's error attached. AUDIT: the write trail records source document hash, extracted values, confidence score, reviewer identity if any, target system response — the full provenance from PDF byte to ERP row; a regulator asking 'where did this number come from' gets a query. AND REVERSIBILITY: where the target supports it, writes are undoable — a retraction flag rather than a delete, the GA-14 delete lesson applied to integrations.

layers.s: Parse layer: pdfplumber / OCR · page text with quality flags
Schema contract · two-pass with text-support check · confidence computed
High confidence → write · low → exception package → reviewer
Idempotent upserts · per-record results · full provenance · reversibility

scenes.narration: The loop's completeness property: every input ends in one of three states — written, reviewed-then-written, or flagged-undeliverable — never lost, never silently swallowed; a daily reconciliation counts documents in versus records out versus queue depth, and the counts must reconcile, the same completeness assertion as AG-10's parallel merges. Throughput shape: the pipeline is QUEUE-DRIVEN — AG-19 — documents arrive, jobs enqueue, workers scale; nightly batches of thousands run at off-peak model rates, GA-25's batch economics. And the system's eval story, AG-18 style: a fixture set of documents with known field values — extraction accuracy per field, reconciliation rates, exception-rate stability — regression-gated like everything else. When this loop runs, the organization stops typing invoices into systems — the oldest data-entry job in existence, quietly retired with its accuracy IMPROVED, because machines extract and humans review the edge, exactly where their attention belongs.

scenes.title: The document loop as a **pattern template**
scenes.sub: What transfers to every extraction-shaped problem
scenes.narration: Step back: this project's shape — parse to text, extract against a typed contract, verify against source, compute confidence, route to humans or systems, audit everything — is a TEMPLATE, not a one-off. The same loop processes: insurance claims — extraction with policy cross-checks; onboarding documents — ID fields with format validation; compliance filings — figures with regulatory rule checks; support attachments — issue classification with routing. The schema changes, the invariants change, the target systems change; the architecture doesn't. What makes the template transfer: every component was built to be content-agnostic — the parse layer abstracts document format, the contract layer abstracts business shape, the confidence layer abstracts judgment quality. When the next extraction problem arrives — and in any real organization, it arrives quarterly — the project isn't rebuilt; it's INSTANTIATED. That's the deepest lesson of the hands-on stage: the capstones aren't five separate builds; they're one architecture, specialized five ways.

items.s: Parse layer, contract layer, confidence layer — each abstracts its concern · new document type = new schema, not new system
Known-field document sets per type · per-field accuracy · exception-rate regression gates
Claims, onboarding, filings, attachments — the same loop, instantiated · build once, specialize forever

scenes.narration: The build order for this capstone: one — the parse layer, tested on your actual document zoo — the scans, the two-column layouts, the photographed invoices; two — the schema plus validators for ONE document type, end to end; three — the verification pass and confidence computation, tuned on a fixture set until the accept/review split is right — target: auto-accept only what you'd bet on; four — the review package UI, built with the actual reviewers — their seconds-per-review is the metric; five — the idempotent write layer plus reconciliation counts; six — evals and thresholds regression-gated in CI. Each milestone ships value alone: even milestone two beats manual entry for its one type. One project remains in the stage — the messaging assistant — where the same disciplines meet a conversational surface and real users.

scenes.title: Back-office mastered. Now the front door: users, in chat.

recap: Extraction is contract-driven: typed schemas with code validators, two-pass extraction with text-support verification, confidence computed from independent signals
The exception queue routes by computed confidence and serves side-by-side review packages; corrections feed the golden set and pipeline improvements
Integration writes are idempotent upserts with per-record results, full provenance, and reversibility; the whole loop is a content-agnostic template for every extraction problem

quiz.q: Why run a separate verification pass after extraction?
opts: Extraction's signature failure is the plausible-but-unsupported field — a different question ('is it in the text?') catches what the first pass invents
quiz.why: Extraction and audit are different jobs: the extractor finds values, the verifier checks them against the source — separation catches hallucinated plausibility.

quiz.q: Why must exception routing use computed confidence rather than the model's self-assessment?
opts: Models that extract wrongly usually believe they're right — computed scores from validation, verification, and parse quality are independent of that optimism
quiz.why: The same external-verification principle as GA-25's routing: confidence must come from evidence, not from the thing being evaluated.

quiz.q: What makes the daily reconciliation (documents in = records out + queue depth) essential?
opts: Completeness is a first-class invariant — inputs that vanish silently are the extraction system's worst failure, and the counts make that impossible
quiz.why: Every input must end in a known state — written, reviewed, or flagged; the reconciliation is the assertion that proves it.

code.title: The extraction loop, one function
code.body:
async def process_document(pdf_path: str) -> Route:
    pages = parse_layer.extract(pdf_path)          # text + quality flags
    record, issues = await extract_and_verify(pages)
    conf = confidence(record_valid=record is not None,
                      verify_issues=issues,
                      parse_quality=pages.quality)

    if conf >= AUTO_ACCEPT and record:
        result = await systems.upsert(record, key=record.natural_key())
        audit.log(hash(pdf_path), record, conf, result)
        return Route("written", result)

    package = review_package(pdf=pdf_path, record=record,
                             issues=issues, confidence=conf)
    await exception_queue.push(package)            # human decides
    audit.log(hash(pdf_path), record, conf, "queued")
    return Route("review", package.id)

# Invariants: idempotent (natural keys) · complete (reconciled counts) ·
# provenance (audit from byte to row) · learning (corrections → gold).
annot: confidence() combines independent signals — no single failure mode can fake high confidence
review_package carries everything: the reviewer's seconds-per-case is a designed metric
Both branches audit: auto-acceptance is a decision too, and it's sampled for audit

notes:
# Project: Document Processing Agent

## Extraction
- Parse layer (pdfplumber/OCR) upstream · typed schema contract (Pydantic + code validators).
- Two-pass: extract then verify text-support · confidence computed (validation + verification + parse quality).

## Exception queue
- Computed-confidence routing · side-by-side packages with per-field issues · corrections → golden cases + pipeline fixes.
- Metrics: exception rate, issue classes, correction rate · sampled audit of auto-accepts.

## Integration
- Idempotent upserts (natural keys) · per-record results · full provenance audit · reversibility.
- Queue-driven throughput · daily reconciliation (in = out + queued).

## Template
- Content-agnostic: parse / contract / confidence layers · instantiate per document type (claims, onboarding, filings).
- Build order: parse → one schema E2E → confidence tuning → review UI → writes + reconciliation → evals.
